subject: Aligning breach notice windows and cooperation obligations for healthcare customers - Crescent Health
messages:

Cc: CloudInfra Solutions <security@cloudinfra.com>

Subject: Question on breach-notify timing & cooperation obligations under DPA

Hi Kimberly,

We're finalizing Crescent Health's vendor intake and have a couple of specific questions about the incident/notification language in your DPA. As a healthcare customer (HIPAA scope), we need clarity on two points before we sign:

1) Timing: our legal team expects vendor notice to customers "without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of discovery". Is Redwood able to commit to a 72-hour notice window to customers (or to provide us immediate notification so we can satisfy our obligations)?

2) Cooperation: in the event of a breach affecting our data, what level of forensic cooperation and evidence preservation will you provide (logs, preserved images, access for our third-party forensics vendor)? Any restrictions on sharing (e.g., export controls, redaction) we should be aware of?

Please point us to the DPA section and any sample language you prefer. For HIPAA customers, we also need confirmation about law-enforcement carve-outs and whether you will delay customer notice if required by law enforcement.

Appreciate a short note and any attachments you can share (SOC 2 sections, typical response timelines).

Thanks,

Senior Counsel, Crescent Health

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers below and I attached a SOC 2 excerpt plus our proposed notify language for your review.

1) Timing — Redwood's baseline (per our standard DPA): we will notify the customer "without undue delay after becoming aware of a confirmed security incident affecting Customer Data". We typically aim to provide initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware, and follow with a substantive update within 5 business days. We do not commit to a 72-hour window for unconfirmed/ongoing investigations because we avoid premature notices that could be misleading.

2) Cooperation — we provide forensic artifacts and preserved logs on request, subject to legal constraints and data minimization (we redact unrelated customer content). We will:
- Preserve relevant logs and system images for a reasonable preservation period;
- Provide time-stamped logs, packet captures (when available), and a summary of affected components;
- Coordinate secure transfer to an agreed third-party forensics vendor (SLA and access control apply).

Law enforcement: we comply with lawful requests and may agree to a reasonable delay for customer notice if a recognized law enforcement agency requests it in writing; we will aim to give the customer as much notice as permitted.

I've attached: redwood_SOC2_section12.pdf (incident response controls) and proposed-notify-language.docx (draft clause we usually provide to healthcare customers).

If helpful, Rafael and Priyom are looped in for any contract-level redlines. Proposed next step: if you send your preferred DPA snippet, we'll propose explicit redline language against it (quick turn).

Best,

Kim — quick thoughts:
- I think we should avoid an absolute "72 hours from discovery" commitment. Instead, propose: "initial notification within 72 hours of confirmation that Customer Data was affected, absent lawful delay". That gives us room during triage.
- We should also call out the scope of "forensic cooperation" (e.g., preservation of logs for 90 days, export format, access windows) so Crescent's forensics vendor knows what to expect.

I'll draft a tightened clause unless Priyom prefers to take it. If client pushes, we can offer a limited SLA credit for failure to meet substantive update timelines rather than a strict penalty tied to first notice.

-Rafa

Hi all — agreed with Rafael's framing. For convenience I've pasted a proposed paragraph below that narrows ambiguity and is operationally implementable: feel free to redline.

"Incident notification and cooperation. Redwood will (a) notify Customer without undue delay and, where feasible, provide an initial notification within seventy‑two (72) hours after Redwood confirms that Customer Data has been impacted by a security incident; (b) provide substantive status updates at reasonable intervals and a final incident report summarizing root cause, affected data types, and mitigations; (c) preserve and make available relevant logs, system snapshots, and chain‑of‑custody records to Customer or Customer's designated forensic vendor for a period of up to ninety (90) days upon request; and (d) comply with lawful requests from law enforcement which may require a temporary delay in customer notification, provided Redwood will use reasonable efforts to notify Customer as soon as legally permitted. Redwood's obligations to preserve or transfer data are subject to applicable law and reasonable security and privacy safeguards (e.g., redaction of unrelated customer content)."

Operational notes: 72 hours is tied to confirmation of impact (not preliminary detection). Preservation window of 90 days is typical and gives us time to scope and prepare transfer. We should add a sentence about cost recovery for extensive on-site support or forensics if the activity is outside standard support.

Happy to convert this into a tracked redline against Crescent's DPA excerpt.
